elements.quote: Weincludedrandomisedtrials in people with suspected, probable, or confirmed covid-19 that compared blood products and covid-19-specific antiviral antibodies against one another or against no intervention, placebo, or standard care.
elements.reason: The eligibility criteria implicitly convey the PICO (population: people with covid-19; interventions: blood products and covid-19-specific antibodies; comparators: each other, no intervention, placebo, or standard care; outcomes listed), but no explicit planned-comparisons statement framed in PICO form is reported; it must be inferred from eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: We included randomised trials in people with suspected, probable, or confirmed covid-19 that compared blood products and covid-19-specific antiviral antibodies against one another or against no intervention, placebo, or standard care... No restrictions were applied based on severity of illness or setting.
elements.reason: Eligible designs (randomised trials), population, interventions, comparators, and setting are all explicitly specified; exclusion of non-randomised trials and other intervention types is also stated.

elements.quote: We included trials regardless of publication status (peer reviewed, in press, or preprint) or language.
elements.reason: Publication status and language restrictions are explicitly addressed (none applied), confirming report-characteristic eligibility criteria.
The manuscript does not distinguish between excluding studies because outcomes were not measured versus outcomes not being reported; no such distinction appears in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: We included randomised trials... that compared blood products and covid-19-specific antiviral antibodies against one another or against no intervention, placebo, or standard care... We meta-analysed interventions with ≥100 patients randomised or ≥20 events per treatment arm.
elements.reason: Intervention groups and comparisons are specified (text_15, text_6), and a synthesis grouping threshold is given (text_6, callout_0), but the full list of intervention nodes/groups used in each synthesis is not fully enumerated in the retrieved methods evidence.

elements.quote: limited meta-analysis of interventions that were randomised to at least 100 patients (or had ≥20 events) to avoid spurious or imprecise findings with network meta-analysis
elements.reason: A rationale is provided for the notable restriction on synthesis eligibility (minimum sample/event thresholds), and text_15 also explains why certain trial types (vaccines, prophylaxis) were handled separately.

elements.quote: We searched WHO information sources from 1 December 2019 to 21 July 2021, and the Chinese literature from inception to 20 February 2021.
elements.reason: Search dates for each source are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Medline (Ovid and PubMed), PubMed Central, Embase, CAB Abstracts, Global Health, PsycInfo, Cochrane Library, Scopus, ...

elements.quote: ClinicalTrials.gov, bioRxiv (preprints), medRxiv (preprints), chemRxiv (preprints), and SSRN (preprints)
elements.reason: Registers/repositories such as ClinicalTrials.gov and preprint servers are named within the WHO database description, but name-specific date restrictions are only given at the aggregate level (text_4: up to 21 July 2021), not per register.

elements.quote: WHO covid-19 website, CDC covid-19 website

No evidence that individuals were contacted to identify studies.
No mention of reference list examination as an information source.
No backward or forward citation searching reported in the retrieved evidence.
No journals or conference proceedings were directly consulted as sources.

elements.quote: Aprotocol provides the detailed methods of this systematic review, including all updates (see supplementary data on bmj.com).
elements.reason: Databases and sources are named (WHO covid-19 database, CDC database, six Chinese databases, L-OVE, living evidence services), and the Chinese search strategy is said to be in the supplement, but the full search strategies as run for every database are not presented in the retrieved text; they are deferred to the protocol/supplementary material.

elements.quote: Wesearched WHO information sources from 1 December 2019 to 21 July 2021, and the Chinese literature from inception to 20 February 2021.
elements.reason: Search limits such as date restrictions and the RCT filter ('we filter the results from the WHO database through a validated and highly sensitive machine learning model') are described, but the limits are not explicitly justified by reference to the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: We adapted the search terms for covid-19 developed by the CDC to the Chinese language.
elements.reason: A published search approach (CDC covid-19 search terms) is cited and its adaptation to Chinese, including added RCT search terms, is described.

elements.quote: To identify randomised controlled trials, we filter the results from the WHO database through a validated and highly sensitive machine learning model.

No tools used to translate search strings between databases or sources are mentioned in the retrieved evidence.
No validation of the search strategy or validation studies are described in the retrieved evidence.
No peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) is reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: pairs of reviewers, following training and calibration exercises, extract data independently using a standardised, pilot tested data extraction form
elements.reason: Pairs of reviewers collect data.

elements.quote: pairs of reviewers ... extract data independently
elements.reason: Independent duplicate extraction reported.

elements.quote: Reviewers resolve discrepancies by discussion and, when necessary, with adjudication by a third party.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution described.
No mention of obtaining or confirming data from study investigators.
No automation tools for data collection described; Covidence was for screening only.
No evidence of translation needs; conditional and not reported.
No evidence figure extraction was needed.
No decision rules for multiple reports or inconsistencies reported.

elements.quote: Selected outcomes include mortality (closest to 90 days), mechanical ventilation (total number of patients, over 90 days), adverse events leading to discontinuation (within 28 days), viral clearance (closest to 7 days ±3 days), transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI; total number of patients, within 28 days), transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO; total number of patients, within 28 days), infusion reactions (total number of patients, within 28 days), duration of hospitalisation, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, time to symptom resolution or clinical improvement, and time to viral clearance.
elements.reason: The outcomes of interest are comprehensively listed with definitions (e.g. TRALI, TACO) and rationale for some (viral clearance as surrogate for transmissibility).

elements.quote: mortality (closest to 90 days), mechanical ventilation (total number of patients, over 90 days), adverse events leading to discontinuation (within 28 days), viral clearance (closest to 7 days ±3 days)
elements.reason: Time frames are specified for most outcomes; some outcomes (e.g. duration of hospitalisation, ICU length of stay) are inherently time-based measures without an additional time point needed.

elements.quote: outcomes of interest (means or medians and measures of variability for continuous outcomes and the number of participants analysed and the number of participants who experienced an event for dichotomous outcomes)
elements.reason: The types of results collected are described, but the manuscript does not explicitly state whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.
No evidence indicates that only a subset of compatible results was selected; no selection process is described and no statement suggests it was needed.

elements.quote: A protocol provides the detailed methods of this systematic review, including all updates (see supplementary data on bmj.com).
elements.reason: No changes to outcome domains are reported in the retrieved evidence; the living review updates are handled in the protocol/supplementary data, and no such changes are documented in the provided text.
No evidence of changes to result-selection processes within outcome domains is reported.

elements.quote: the review team chose thresholds of small but important effects by consensus: 1% for mortality, 2% for mechanical ventilation, 1% for hospitalisation, 1 day for duration of hospitalisation, and 2% for all adverse effects
elements.reason: Key outcomes for interpreting conclusions (mortality, mechanical ventilation, hospitalisation, adverse effects) are identified with rationale (consensus thresholds of minimal importance).

elements.quote: Reviewers collect information on trial characteristics (trial registration, publication status, study status, design), patient characteristics (country, age, sex, smoking habits, comorbidities, setting and type of care, severity of covid-19 symptoms, timing of therapy relative to symptom onset), donor characteristics (selection criteria, sex, severity of disease), and outcomes of interest (means or medians and measures of variability for continuous outcomes and the number of participants analysed and the number of participants who experienced an event for dichotomous outcomes).
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists and defines the variables sought (trial, patient, and donor characteristics and outcome data) using a standardised, pilot-tested extraction form.
No evidence in the retrieved text describes assumptions made about missing or unclear study information during data collection.

elements.quote: Outcomes of interest were selected based on the clinical expertise of our systematic review team and by a guideline panel developing WHO and BMJ Rapid Recommendations.
elements.reason: Data items were selected by expert/panel consensus rather than with any tool, so no tool citation applies; the evidence supports this.

elements.quote: use a revision of the Cochrane tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials (RoB 2.0) 28 to rate trials
elements.reason: The tool (RoB 2.0, a revision of the Cochrane risk of bias tool) is explicitly named, with reference 28 to Sterne et al.

elements.quote: across the following domains: bias arising from the randomisation process; bias owing to departures from the intended intervention; bias from missing outcome data; bias in measurement of the outcome; bias in selection of the reported results, including deviations from the registered protocol; bias due to competing risks; and bias arising from early termination for benefit
elements.reason: All domains assessed by the tool are enumerated.

elements.quote: We rate trials at high risk of bias overall if one or more domains were rated as (c) someconcerns, probably high risk of bias or as (d) high risk of bias, and as low risk of bias overall if all domains were rated as ( b ) some concerns, probably low risk of bias or ( a ) low risk of bias.
elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias judgement is made and the derivation rules are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: use a revision of the Cochrane tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials (RoB 2.0)
elements.reason: The use of a revision/modification of the Cochrane RoB 2.0 tool is described (also 'a modification of the Cochrane risk of bias 2.0 tool' in text_6), though detailed description of the adaptations is limited; the revision is identified and its modified domains and rules are given.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool was used; an existing tool (RoB 2.0) was applied.

elements.quote: reviewers, following training and calibration exercises, use a revision of the Cochrane tool ... Reviewers resolve discrepancies by discussion and, when necessary, with adjudication by a third party.
elements.reason: Multiple reviewers ('pairs' implied by 'reviewers' and third-party adjudication) assess risk of bias, with discrepancy resolution by discussion and third-party adjudication described. Independence is implied by the discrepancy-resolution process but not explicitly stated as independent assessment.
No evidence of processes to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators; this conditional element does not appear to apply.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are reported; the assessment was performed manually by reviewers.

elements.quote: We summarised the effect of interventions on dichotomous outcomes using odds ratios and their corresponding 95% credible interval (CI). For outcomes with extremely rare events, we summarised the effect of interventions using risk difference and 95% CI. For continuous outcomes, specifically duration of hospital stay, we used the mean difference and corresponding 95% CI... For time to symptom resolution, time to viral clearance, and duration of mechanical ventilation, we performed the analyses using ratio of means and corresponding 95% CI before calculating the mean difference in days
elements.reason: The methods specify the effect measure for each outcome type: odds ratios for dichotomous outcomes, risk difference for extremely rare events, mean difference for duration of hospital stay, and ratio of means for time-to-event outcomes.

elements.quote: the review team chose thresholds of small but important effects by consensus: 1% for mortality, 2% for mechanical ventilation, 1% for hospitalisation, 1 day for duration of hospitalisation, and 2% for all adverse effects.
elements.reason: Thresholds for interpreting effect sizes (minimally important differences) are reported along with their rationale (chosen by consensus in the absence of quantitative patient values data).

elements.quote: we performed the analyses using ratio of means and corresponding 95% CI before calculating the mean difference in days... To facilitate interpretation of results of dichotomous outcomes, we calculated absolute effects per 1000 patients.
elements.reason: Re-expression of results is described: ratio of means converted to mean difference in days, and relative effects converted to absolute effects per 1000 patients using specified baseline risks.

elements.quote: we used the mean difference and corresponding 95% CI because we expect similar durations across randomised trials
elements.reason: A justification is given for the mean difference for duration of hospital stay, but no justification is provided for the other effect measure choices (odds ratios, risk difference, ratio of means).

elements.quote: We meta-analysed interventions with ≥100 patients randomised or ≥20 events per treatment arm.
elements.reason: The manuscript partially describes processes deciding which studies were eligible for each synthesis: it specifies a minimum evidence threshold for meta-analysing interventions (text_6: '≥100 patients randomised or ≥20 events per treatment arm') and states that network meta-analysis was performed 'for outcomes with sufficient data' with pairwise meta-analysis otherwise (text_20). However, it does not explicitly describe processes such as tabulating study intervention characteristics and comparing them against planned synthesis groups (e.g., grouping of antibody/cellular therapy classes), so the description is incomplete.

elements.quote: For outcomes where the median risk of an event in the control group was 0 (that is, TACO, TRALI, adverse events leading to discontinuation), we performed network meta-analysis with risk difference and fixed effects rather than odd ratios and random effects... Wedid not perform any adjustments for interventions with zero events.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes some data preparation/handling decisions, notably handling zero-event outcomes by switching to risk differences and fixed effects, and describes a threshold for meta-analysing interventions. However, no methods for handling missing summary statistics or explicit data conversions (e.g., median-to-mean imputation) are reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The supplementary data include network plots and forest plots of pairwise meta-analyses for all outcomes, as well as detailed relative and absolute effect estimates and the certainty of evidence for all comparisons and outcomes.
elements.reason: Supplementary tables of effect estimates and certainty are mentioned, and Table 1 study characteristics, but no explicit description of the tabular structures used to display synthesis results and their contents.

elements.quote: Figure 2 presents a summary of the effects of interventions on important efficacy and safety outcomes. The supplementary data include network plots and forest plots of pairwise meta-analyses for all outcomes
elements.reason: Graphical displays (summary figure, network plots, forest plots) of results are described.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies in tables or figures is reported in the retrieved evidence.
No rationale for using non-standard graphs is reported; the methods in text_16 describe network plot construction but not as a non-standard graph rationale for display of results.

elements.quote: Weperformed a random-effects bayesian meta-analysis using the bayesmeta package 29 in RStudio version 3.5.3 (R Studio, Boston, MA, USA).
elements.reason: Software (RStudio v3.5.3, bayesmeta, gemtc packages) with version numbers reported.

elements.quote: Weperformed bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis for outcomes with sufficient data, and synthesise all other outcomes using pairwise bayesian random-effects meta-analyses if there was only one comparison for a specific outcome.
elements.reason: Alternative synthesis (pairwise meta-analysis) for outcomes lacking sufficient data is described and justified; design also states pairwise MA for outcomes with insufficient data (text_3).

elements.quote: we performed network meta-analysis with risk difference and fixed effects rather than odd ratios and random effects
elements.reason: Random-effects Bayesian model is reported with rationale for switching to fixed effects for specific outcomes.

elements.quote: Weused three Markov chains with 100 000 iterations after an initial burn-in of 10 000 and a thinning of 10. Node splitting models were used to obtain indirect estimates and to assess local heterogeneity.
elements.reason: Statistical methods (Bayesian MCMC, node splitting) are described.

elements.quote: Node splitting models were used to obtain indirect estimates and to assess local heterogeneity.
elements.reason: Heterogeneity assessment via node splitting described; inconsistency assessed in GRADE as well.

elements.quote: we used a plausible prior for the variance parameter
elements.reason: Bayesian analysis specifies variance (between-study heterogeneity) handling via a plausible prior.
No evidence on method for calculating confidence/credible intervals of summary effects.

elements.quote: Wedid not perform any adjustments for interventions with zero events. The R code used is available publicly at https://github.com/covid19lnma/covid19_lnma/.
elements.reason: Additional random-effects/Bayesian implementation details (zero-event handling, publicly available R code) are reported.

elements.quote: we used a plausible prior for the variance parameter and a uniform prior for the effect parameter.
elements.reason: Prior distributions for variance and effect parameters are described.
No retrieved evidence describes methods to account for statistical dependency among multiple estimates from the same study.

elements.quote: For outcomes where the median risk of an event in the control group was 0 (that is, TACO, TRALI, adverse events leading to discontinuation), we performed network meta-analysis with risk difference and fixed effects rather than odd ratios and random effects.
elements.reason: Planned syntheses altered for specific outcomes (zero control events) with reasons reported; pairwise MA used for outcomes with only one comparison (text_20).

elements.quote: Weplan to conduct subgroup analyses based on high versus low risk of bias studies. Additionally, for convalescent plasma, we plan to perform subgroup analyses based on antibody titres and time of infusion relative to disease progression.
elements.reason: Methods to explore heterogeneity via subgroup analyses are explicitly described.

elements.quote: subgroup analyses based on antibody titres and time of infusion relative to disease progression. We hypothesise that treatment with convalescent plasma will be more efficacious when transfusion occurs earlier in the disease course, and when plasma from patients with more severe illness is used.
elements.reason: Factors (risk of bias, antibody titres, infusion timing), levels (high vs low, early vs late), and expected direction of effect modification are reported.
No statement on whether subgroup analyses used study-level variables or within-study contrasts.

elements.quote: When there is statistical evidence of a subgroup effect, we will assess its credibility using the Instrument to assess the Credibility of Effect Modification Analyses in randomised controlled trials and meta-analyses (ICEMAN) tool.
elements.reason: Method for comparing/assessing subgroup effects (ICEMAN tool) is reported.
Meta-analysis was performed; no evidence that informal exploration of heterogeneity without meta-analysis was used.
No identification of which heterogeneity analyses were post hoc versus pre-specified.

The retrieved evidence describes planned subgroup analyses (e.g., by risk of bias, antibody titres, timing of infusion) but does not describe any sensitivity analyses conducted to assess robustness of the synthesised results.
No sensitivity analyses are reported in the retrieved evidence, so there is no statement identifying whether any sensitivity analyses were pre-specified or conducted post hoc.

elements.quote: use a revision of the Cochrane tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials (RoB 2.0) 28 to rate trials as ... across the following domains: bias arising from the randomisation process; bias owing to departures from the intended intervention; bias from missing outcome data; bias in measurement of the outcome; bias in selection of the reported results, including deviations from the registered protocol
elements.reason: Methods to assess risk of bias due to missing outcome data and selection of reported results (reporting biases) are explicitly described as part of the RoB 2.0 assessment.

elements.quote: We rate trials at high risk of bias overall if one or more domains were rated as (c) someconcerns, probably high risk of bias or as (d) high risk of bias, and as low risk of bias overall if all domains were rated as ( b ) some concerns, probably low risk of bias or ( a ) low risk of bias.
elements.reason: The domains assessed and the process for deriving an overall judgement are reported.

elements.quote: We assessed risk of bias using a modification of the Cochrane risk of bias 2.0 tool.
elements.reason: The use of a modified RoB 2.0 tool is mentioned, but the specific adaptations are not fully detailed in the retrieved evidence, beyond listing extra domains (competing risks, early termination).
No newly developed tool; an existing tool (RoB 2.0) was used.

elements.quote: For each eligible trial and outcome, reviewers, following training and calibration exercises, use a revision of the Cochrane tool ... Reviewers resolve discrepancies by discussion and, when necessary, with adjudication by a third party.
elements.reason: Reviewer independence (pairs, after training), and disagreement-resolution via discussion and third-party adjudication are reported.
No evidence of processes to obtain or confirm information from study investigators for reporting-bias assessment; not reported.
No evidence that automation tools were used for reporting-bias assessment; requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: We assessed the certainty of evidence using the grading of recommendations assessment, development, and evaluation (GRADE) approach, 35-37 including specific guidance for network meta-analyses.
elements.reason: The tool (GRADE) and its NMA-specific guidance are explicitly specified.

elements.quote: taking into consideration risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, publication bias, imprecision, incoherence (differences between direct and indirect effect estimates), and intransitivity (differences in study characteristics that may modify the treatment effect in the direct comparisons that form the basis for the indirect estimate)
elements.reason: Factors considered (GRADE domains plus NMA-specific incoherence and intransitivity) are reported with criteria explained.

elements.quote: We rated the certainty for each comparison and outcome as high, moderate, low, or very low
elements.reason: Overall certainty levels (high/moderate/low/very low) and their derivation via GRADE domains are described.

elements.quote: We used a minimally contextualised approach with a null effect threshold to rate the certainty that there is a benefit or a harm... the review team chose thresholds of small but important effects by consensus: 1% for mortality, 2% for mechanical ventilation, 1% for hospitalisation, 1 day for duration of hospitalisation, and 2% for all adverse effects.
elements.reason: Review-specific thresholds and their rationale (consensus, minimally contextualised approach) are reported.

elements.quote: including specific guidance for network meta-analyses
